title: Embed usage cost estimates and billing metadata into Redwood-verified performance profiles
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and internal teams often need a quick, reliable estimate of operating cost (USD/token and USD/1000-requests) when selecting a Redwood-verified performance profile. Current performance profiles contain latency/throughput metrics but lack standardized billing metadata, forcing engineers to stitch telemetry, pricing plans, and batch/quantization knobs together during capacity planning.

Goal: Add machine-readable and human-friendly cost estimates to each verified performance profile. These estimates should reflect typical serving configurations (default batch size, quantization level, KV-cache behavior) and map to Redwood billing units so SREs, platform teams, and product owners can make informed decisions without manual calculation.

Out of scope: Per-customer reserved-capacity discounts, promotional credits, and fine-grain per-region pricing differences. Those will remain covered by price lookup APIs and invoices.
acceptance_criteria: Each verified performance profile (new and refreshed) includes a machine-readable billing section with fields: usd_per_1k_tokens, usd_per_request (baseline), assumptions (batch_size, quantization, seq_len), and confidence_interval_label.
Console displays cost estimate in profile details with an explainer tooltip and link to the precise pricing calculator page.
Profile publish pipeline emits the billing metadata artifact (signed JSON blob) alongside existing performance artifacts; artifact passes schema validation in staging.
SDKs expose cost estimate via profile metadata endpoint and surface warnings when profiles are used with settings that diverge from assumptions (e.g., different batch_size or quantization).
E2E tests validate one sample model (open LLM) profile in staging: generate profile, compute cost estimate, publish artifact, and assert console + SDK read the same numbers.
Documentation entry in Confluence describing assumptions and how to interpret cost estimates is published and linked from the profile UI.
tasks: Define billing metadata schema with finance and runtime: fields + units + recommended assumptions
Implement estimator module in the profile publisher that converts perf telemetry and runtime unit-cost to usd_per_1k_tokens
Update publish pipeline to sign and store billing artifact with profile bundle
Console UX: add cost card, tooltip copy, and link to pricing calculator
SDK: return billing metadata from /profiles/:id endpoint and log warning if runtime params deviate
End-to-end staging test and rollout plan (canary profiles then global)
comments: 2026-02-10 Maya Patel: Created ticket. Initial scope agreed with Finance (A. Gomez) and Runtime (J. Kim) in kickoff. Finance emphasized need for deterministic assumptions and a clear user-facing explainer to avoid bill surprises.

2026-02-17 Jonah Kim: Drafted schema v0.1 and estimator pseudocode. Default assumptions proposed: batch_size=8, quantization=q4_0, seq_len=512, kv_cache_enabled=true. Shared with ENG and Finance for feedback.

2026-02-22 A. Gomez (Finance): Reviewed schema; asked to add 'pricing_model' field to indicate whether estimate is based on per-token or per-request primary billing. Suggested adding a 'variance_bucket' (low/med/high) to communicate confidence.
2026-02-26 Jonah Kim: Updated estimator to consume regional unit-cost rates via pricing-service API. Implemented unit tests and a small CLI to run cost estimate from perf artifact locally.
2026-03-01 Design (Elena R.): Mocked cost card UI and tooltip copy. UX decision: show both usd_per_1k_tokens and usd_per_request, with a single-line caveat linking to docs. Approved by PM.

2026-03-03 Jonah Kim: Pushed PR for estimator and publish-pipeline changes; CI failing on signature packaging step. Spun off ENG-42109 to unblock signing step. Marking this ticket In Progress while we resolve CI and run staging E2E.
notes: Migration: existing profiles will receive a null billing section until they are refreshed; backlog job planned to recompute billing metadata for top-100 profiles by usage.
Operational considerations: billing metadata must be recomputable deterministically during audits. Store the runtime assumptions with the signed artifact.

Risk: mismatch between estimate assumptions and customer runtime (custom quantization or extreme batch sizes) can lead to perceived inaccuracies. Mitigation: clear UI caveats and SDK runtime warnings.
